stem.text: Determine whether \( f(x) = 4 e^{2 x} - 2 \) is the particular solution to the differential equation \( \frac{dy}{dx} = 2 y + 4 \) with the initial condition \( f(0) = 3 \). Justify your answer.

answer_key.label: No. \( f^{\prime}(x) = 2\left(f(x) + 2\right) \) for every x, but \( f(0) = 2 \), not 3.

worked_solution.text: Differentiate the candidate: \( f^{\prime}(x) = 8 e^{2 x} \).
Substitute into the right side: \( 2\left(f(x) + 2\right) = 8 e^{2 x} \), which equals \( f^{\prime}(x) \) for every x, so f satisfies the differential equation.
Check the initial condition: \( f(0) = 2 \), which is not 3, so f is not the particular solution.

options.label: No. \( f^{\prime}(x) \ne 2\left(f(x) + 2\right) \) for the candidate, so f is not a solution of the equation.
options.derivation: failure of the equation asserted with no input exhibited, when the equation in fact holds
